assessments.support: 871-subject ABIDE I cohort (403 ASD, 468 controls) from 20 sites, same well-documented subset as Abraham et al. 2017.
C-PAC pipeline and Harvard-Oxford (110-ROI) atlas explicitly specified.
Diagnostic label inherited from ABIDE phenotypic file; no diagnostic instrument/criteria restated in this short conference paper.

Siamese network trained on matching/non-matching subject pairs, with subjects from all 20 sites present in both training and test sets rather than held out; k = 3 and other network hyperparameters tuned via cross-validation but pair-based splitting makes independence between train/test pairs unclear.

risk_of_bias.summary: Short, methodologically transparent conference paper reusing the well-characterised 871-subject ABIDE cohort; main appraisal concerns are the pair-based (not subject-independent, not site-held-out) train/test construction typical of metric-learning setups.

charting.title: Distance Metric Learning Using Graph Convolutional Networks: Application to Functional Brain Networks
charting.authors: Ktena SI; Parisot S; Ferrante E; Rajchl M; Lee M; Glocker B; Rueckert D
charting.feature_types: functional connectivity graph (brain graph with Harvard-Oxford ROI nodes)
charting.specific_features: Functional connectivity edges between Harvard-Oxford ROIs; k-NN anatomical graph structure for spectral convolution
charting.specific_algorithms: Siamese GCN distance-metric learning compared with a simple k-nn classifier (k=3) on learned distances vs. Euclidean/PCA distances
charting.validation_methodology: Random subject/pair split into training and test sets ensuring all 20 sites present in both; network hyperparameters tuned via cross-validation
charting.performance_metrics: k-nn classification accuracy (per-site and all-sites), AUC/ROC
charting.key_performance_results: k-nn (k=3) accuracy on the GCN-learned metric: 62.9% across all sites (vs. 51.0% for PCA/Euclidean distance), an 11.9 percentage-point improvement; larger per-site gains for some of the 5 biggest sites (e.g. site 18: 90.0% vs 50.0%)
charting.summary_key_findings: A siamese graph convolutional network learns a graph-similarity metric for ABIDE functional connectomes that improves k-nn ASD-vs-control classification accuracy by 11.9 percentage points (62.9% vs. 51.0%) over a traditional PCA/Euclidean distance metric, with larger gains within individual sites than across all sites pooled.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I; 871 subjects (403 ASD, 468 controls) from 20 sites
narrative_row.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed Harvard-Oxford (110-ROI) connectivity graphs; siamese graph convolutional network learning a graph-distance metric from matching/non-matching subject pairs; k-nn (k=3) classification on learned distances compared to PCA/Euclidean distance
narrative_row.outcomes: k-nn accuracy 62.9% across all sites with the learned GCN metric vs. 51.0% with PCA/Euclidean distance (11.9-point improvement); larger per-site improvements (e.g. site 18: 90.0% vs 50.0%); AUC improvements reported per site
narrative_row.key_limitations: Pair-based siamese training/testing with all 20 sites represented in both splits rather than held out; short conference format limits detail on diagnostic label source and on leakage control for pair construction
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A graph-metric-learning method applied to the same well-characterised 871-subject ABIDE cohort used elsewhere in this corpus, useful for linking methodological lineage in the dataset-publication graph
